title: WoW Jumped From 7.4 to 10 Million Subscribers in 7 Weeks
hook: In November 2014 Warlords of Draenor pushed World of Warcraft from 7.4 million subscribers back past 10 million, and the servers buckled so badly Blizzard handed out five free days. Were you stuck in that queue?
script: Did you know World of Warcraft once gained more than two and a half million subscribers in about seven weeks? At the end of September twenty fourteen, Blizzard's parent company reported seven point four million subscribers. Earlier that year the count had dipped to six point eight million, its lowest in years. Then Warlords of Draenor launched on November thirteenth. The expansion sold through more than three point three million copies in its first twenty four hours. By that same day, Blizzard said, the subscriber count had climbed back past ten million. It announced the number six days later. The launch itself was rough. Servers were overcrowded, queues stretched for hours, and players who got in faced lag and disconnects. Blizzard lowered realm population caps to keep things stable, which made the waits even longer. Executive producer J Allen Brack posted an apology and gave every active subscriber five free days of game time. The surge did not last. The following year Blizzard reported the count had fallen again, and then it stopped publishing subscriber numbers for good. So Warlords holds a strange record. It was the last expansion to ever show a public subscriber jump. Were you in that queue in twenty fourteen? Follow for more gaming history.
